title: NaN/Inf from sqrt of small negative eigenvalues of the Coulomb matrix; sqrt_coulomb_threshold must be 0
symptom: The auxiliary-basis Coulomb matrix (mat_coulomb) has small negative eigenvalues from numerical error, which turn into NaN when the square root is taken. The user flagged that the filtering threshold before the sqrt must default to 0 and asked to verify it.
root_cause: The Coulomb matrix is not exactly positive semi-definite numerically, so an unfiltered negative eigenvalue passed to sqrt yields NaN. The code relies on sqrt_coulomb_threshold (default 0) to filter negative/near-singular eigen-directions - and that filtering lives in whichever eigen-solver branch is actually taken (ELPA vs ScaLAPACK power_hemat_blacs_real), so a run on the other branch can leave negative eigenvalues unfiltered.
minimal_fix: Verify sqrt_coulomb_threshold is 0 (its intended default), determine from the run log which eigen-solver branch was actually executed (ELPA vs ScaLAPACK power_hemat_blacs_real), and confirm negative eigen-directions are filtered before the square root. If the log shows unfiltered negative eigenvalues, fix that branch's filtering instead of editing the Coulomb matrix.
validation: Grep the run log for unfiltered-negative-eigenvalue warnings and check outputs for NaN/Inf: with sqrt_coulomb_threshold=0 and the correct branch, negative eigen-directions are filtered and the sqrt/inverse step stays finite.
avoid: Do not equate a negative eigenvalue of the Coulomb matrix with a broken input or with NaN by itself - negative eigenvalues of mat_coulomb are normal numerical error. Do not 'fix' it by shifting or regularizing the matrix before the sqrt; threshold filtering is the intended mechanism.

parameters.sqrt_coulomb_threshold: 0 (default; filters negative/near-singular eigen-directions before the sqrt)
